public_rationale: The forecast has no deadline. Later company disclosures describe substantial advances across relevant tasks, so the claim cannot be treated as supported merely because earlier systems were limited. The examined records do not independently establish the complete assistant capability or rule out its eventual development. No decisive event meets the early-resolution rule.
limitations: The metaphor leaves the capability threshold partly dependent on interpretation.
Company performance claims are not equivalent to independent confirmation.
Available independent evaluations cover only portions of the proposed capability.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative AI will not become the incredible supercomputer Altman has promised.

statement.excerpt: Generative artificial intelligence is not going to become the incredible supercomputer that Altman has regularly promised.

from_speaker: the incredible supercomputer that Altman has regularly promised
a super smart person that knows everything about you
our_interpretation: Read the metaphor through the surrounding description: a broadly capable, human-like intelligent assistant that uses personal context and carries out varied tasks.
This concerns functional capability. It does not require biological thought, consciousness, literal omniscience, or error-free performance.
The quoted sentence sets no deadline. The adjacent word imminently supplies no calendar deadline for this broader forecast.
Strong performance on individual benchmarks is relevant but does not alone establish the complete assistant capability.
criteria.support_condition: A decisive technical result establishes that generative AI cannot attain the described functional capability. Present shortcomings or the passage of a finite amount of time are insufficient.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A generative AI system demonstrably functions as the broadly capable, personalized assistant described, with independent verification across varied unfamiliar tasks and sustained use.

evidence.excerpt: “What you really want,” he told MIT Technology Review, “is just this thing that is off helping you.”
evidence.locator: Opening interview section, paragraph beginning with this quotation
evidence.explanation: The firsthand interview describes Altman's prospective assistant vision. It helps identify the forecast's referent but is not evidence that the capability was achieved.

evidence.excerpt: Astra is state-of-the-art on computer use, browsing, software engineering, cybersecurity, science, and professional work.
evidence.explanation: The announcement describes broad capabilities relevant to the forecast and weighs against dismissing progress. It remains a company account and does not independently establish the full personalized-assistant criterion.

evidence.excerpt: You shouldn’t treat our reporting as a complete record of the most capable models.
evidence.locator: FAQ: Why has METR reported time horizons for some models but not others?
evidence.explanation: METR cautions that its coverage is incomplete and explains that its tasks primarily concern software, machine learning, and cybersecurity. Its measurements cannot establish either universal incapability or achievement of the entire assistant vision.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A dated, independently verified system meeting the broadly capable personalized-assistant criterion would contradict the forecast. A decisive technical impossibility result would support it.
